sentences.text:
Author: T. Vinod Kumar
Bench: T. Vinod Kumar
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar
 Writ Petition No.91 Of 2024
Order:

Heard learned Counsel for the petitioner, learned Government Pleader appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 4, Sri L. Prabhakar Reddy, learned Standing Counsel appearing for respondent Nos.6 and 7,
Sri T.S. Praveen Kumar, learned Counsel appearing for respondent No.8 and perused the record.

2. The case of the petitioner, in brief, is that the husband of the 8th respondent had entered into an agreement of sale dated 30.06.2006 with the petitioner for sale of his land admeasuring Ac.5.12 gts.
in Sy. No.155/33 (kasra pahani Sy. No.155/6) situated at Mucherla village, Kandukur Mandal, Ranga Reddy District; that the husband of the 8th respondent had deceased on 17.11.2009; that pending execution of the sale deed, the petitioner was put in possession of the subject land; and that the petitioner taking advantage of the subject land being acquired by the respondent authorities for the benefit of respondent Nos.6 and 7 is seeking to claim compensation amount in respect of the said land which she is not entitled.

3. It is also the further contention of the petitioner that due to non-execution of formal sale deed in her favour by the 8th respondent's husband during his life time, the subject land stands in the name of the 8th respondent's husband and for the said reason, the respondent authorities have shown the name of the husband of the 8th respondent in the land acquisition proceedings initiated and also the Award passed on 28.11.2022; that for the said reason the petitioner had approached the respondent authority and submitted representation bringing to the notice of the authorities the aforesaid facts and sought for not disbursing the compensation amount to the 8th respondent in furtherance of the Award dated 28.11.2023 and that inspite of the petitioner bringing the above facts to the notice of the respondent authorities, they are proceeding to disburse the compensation amount in respect of the subject land in favour of the 8th respondent, which action it is contended is highly illegal and arbitrary.
4.
Counter-affidavit on behalf of the official respondents is not filed.
Counter-affidavit on behalf of the 8th respondent is filed.

5. Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition however, submits that the respondent authorities having passed an Award and noting the objection made by the petitioner, have made a reference as to the apportionment of the compensation amount to the authority in exercise of powers under Section 77(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation, and Transparency in Land Mrs. Sunkati Sailaja vs State Of Telangana on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74190358/
1 Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act'), as the respondent authority cannot go into title disputes.

sentences.text:
6. Learned Government Pleader further submits that the authorities have made reference under Section 77 of the Act to the authority constituted under Section 64 of the Act on 02.08.2024 by depositing the amount of compensation payable in respect of the land admeasuring Ac.5.12 gts. in Sy. No.155/3 of Mucherla revenue village, Kandukur Mandal for the said authority under Section 64 of the Act to decide as to the apportionment of the said compensation amount between the petitioner and the 8th respondent herein.
7.

The 8th respondent by the counter-affidavit had denied the writ averments as to the execution of the sale agreement and the petitioner being put in possession of the subject land and thus being entitled to claim compensation amount pursuant to the acquisition proceedings initiated by the respondents and the Award passed thereafter on 28.11.2022.
8. I have taken note of the respective contentions urged.

9. Admittedly there is an inter se dispute between the petitioner and the 8th respondent in relation to the subject land which has been acquired by the respondent authorities by initiating land acquisition proceedings by issuing preliminary notification under Section 11 of the Act on 20.09.2016 which culminated with passing of Award dated 28.11.2022.
10.

Under the provisions of the Act, whenever there is a dispute with regard to the person entitled to receive compensation shall not consent to receive it, or if there be no person competent to alienate the land, or if there be any dispute as to the title to receive the compensation or as to the apportionment of it, the authority is required to make a reference by depositing the compensation with the authority under Section 64 of the Act.

In the facts of the present case, since there is a dispute relating to apportionment of the compensation amount between the petitioner and the 8th respondent, the acquisition authority is required to deposit the amount of compensation with the authority under Section 64 of the Act, so that the said authority would adjudicate as to the entitlement between the rival claimants.

Though the respondent authority was required to undertake the aforesaid exercise on passing of the Award on 28.11.2022 by depositing the amount,
the acquisition authority did not undertake such exercise immediately.

However, as it is now submitted to the Court that the acquisition authority having deposited the compensation amount with the authority under Section 64 of the Act by exercising powers the authority under Section 77 of the Act, and the Authority under Section 64 of the Act being seized of the matter in relation to adjudication as to the rival claim between the petitioner and the 8th respondent, this Court is of the view that grievance of the petitioner not to disburse the compensation amount to 8th respondent stands addressed.

11. Since the respondent authorities have already deposited the amount with the authority constituted under Section 64 of the Act, it is open for the petitioner to establish her claim before the authority as to her entitlement/claim to receive the compensation amount in respect of the land acquired by the respondent under the Award dated 28.11.2022.
